intro: Welcome to Yarımburgaz Cave, a cave in İstanbul province whose story begins in the Lower Palaeolithic. It is one of Thrace's longest caves, and it holds two very different chapters: in its Lower Palaeolithic layers, the oldest human traces around the Sea of Marmara; in its upper ones, a Byzantine church.
history: The cave overlooks Lake Küçükçekmece. It has two storeys, runs for more than a kilometre and is among the largest in Thrace. In its Lower Palaeolithic layers, stone tools and cave-bear bones record the oldest human presence around the Sea of Marmara. Much later, in Byzantine times, a church was cut into its upper levels.
highlights: As you explore, don't miss the Lower Palaeolithic layers, the remains of the cave bear, the Byzantine church and the two-storey gallery system.
facts: Did you know? For years the cave was used as a quarry and as a mushroom farm, and part of its archaeological sequence was destroyed before it could be excavated. Its Lower Palaeolithic layers record the oldest human presence around the Sea of Marmara. And in its upper levels a Byzantine church was cut: the same cave, used twice, hundreds of thousands of years apart.
outro: This brings our tour of Yarımburgaz Cave to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water. Few places hold so much time in one hollow of rock — thank you for walking through it with us. Enjoy your visit.
